verdicts.EdgeScout:
1. `.foo { color:red; .bar{} @media (max-width:800px){ color:green } }` scoped with empty nested `.bar`
2. `.foo { @media { color:green } }` with null/missing media query params
3. `.foo { @media (max-width:800px){} }` with empty at-rule body plus empty `.bar{}`
4. `.foo { @supports (display:grid){ @media (max-width:800px){ color:green } } }` and `@media (max-width:800px){ .foo{ color:green } }` top-level
5. `.foo { @container (min-width:400px){ color:green } }`, `@supports`, `@layer`, `@starting-style`, `@keyframes` inside scoped `.foo`
6. `.foo { &{} @media (max-width:800px){ color:green } }` vs unicode selector `.foo-日本語 { .bar{} @media (max-width:800px){ color:green } }`
APPROVE
verdicts.FormalAdversaryCritic:
- Specificity/cascade still changes for the common case: `.foo[data-v-x]` has the id in its last compound, so the wrapper remains `&[data-v-x]`; `&` already expands to the scoped parent, and the duplicated attribute makes nested declarations beat later equal-specificity direct declarations.
- Fully `:global(...)` selectors are mis-scoped: by `OnceExit` the `:global` marker has been rewritten away and no id remains, so the string checks miss it and the default `&[id]` incorrectly requires the scope id; mixed selector lists are also decided from the whole string/last whitespace-separated token rather than per selector.
- Pseudo-element handling is incomplete: the `::` test misses legacy single-colon pseudo-elements such as `:before`, `:after`, `:first-line`, and `:first-letter`, for which `&[id]` can place an attribute after the pseudo-element and be dropped.
- The last-compound heuristic is selector-list and syntax fragile: splitting only on whitespace/`>+~` ignores commas and treats functional-pseudo or attribute contents as compounds, so global/deep/slotted branches can be incorrectly scoped or inconsistently handled depending on selector order.
- The empty-rule, missing-params, unicode, and doubly nested grouping cases do not crash, and keyframes/grouping-whitelist/interleaving fixes help, but they do not mitigate the specificity, global, or pseudo-element regressions above.

REVISE
